title: What is Basic Reflex?
subtitle: A practice space, not a fight club

engines.body: The gym as physical environment — small, intentional, every piece of equipment has a purpose
engines.mind: Diagnostic coaching — Coach Paul reads the student, not the syllabus
engines.emotion: Practice space, not fight club. Safe to fail. Community built on shared discipline

audience.hook: Most gyms teach you to hit things. We teach you to think.
audience.question: What makes this gym different from every other boxing gym?

core.thesis: Basic Reflex is a practice space that teaches boxing as a thinking discipline — not a fight club that sells aggression.
keyPoints: Practice space, not fight club — the distinction is the identity
Cuban method applied in Hong Kong: fundamentals, footwork, angles, counter-punching
Diagnostic coaching: Coach Paul reads each student individually — what they need, not what the schedule says
Small and intentional — not a factory. Every student is seen
Boxing as a vehicle for body, mind, and emotional development — the Three Engines
The 10-Block system: structured progression from awareness to mastery
Equipment serves the method, not the other way around — every bag, every drill has a purpose
You don't need to want to fight to train here. Most members never spar.
commonMisconceptions: Boxing gyms are intimidating — BR is built for anyone willing to learn
You need to be fit first — the training makes you fit
It's about fighting — it's about mastering yourself through boxing fundamentals

coachEye.observe: Watch a new student in their first session — what are they afraid of?
coachEye.compare: Compare their movement in week 1 vs week 4 — the stance tells you everything
coachEye.predict: The students who stay are the ones who feel SEEN, not just trained
coachEye.diagnose: If someone leaves early, it's usually because they felt like a number, not a student

scenes.title: Not a Fight Club
scenes.narration: This is not a fight club. There are no cage matches. No one screaming at you to push harder. This is a practice space.
scenes.learningObjective: Establish identity: practice space, not fight club

scenes.title: The Method
scenes.narration: We teach the Cuban school of boxing. Fundamentals. Footwork. Angles. Counter-punching. A system that's been producing world-class boxers for decades — adapted for anyone willing to learn.
scenes.learningObjective: Connect BR to Cuban method (lesson 1 bridge)

scenes.title: Diagnostic Coaching
scenes.narration: Every student is different. Different body. Different fears. Different goals. Coach Paul doesn't follow a script — he reads the student. What do you need right now? Not what does the schedule say.

scenes.title: The Three Engines
scenes.narration: Boxing trains three engines simultaneously. Body — stance, movement, coordination. Mind — timing, angles, reading your opponent. Emotion — composure under pressure, confidence through competence.

scenes.title: The 10 Blocks
scenes.narration: Ten blocks. From awareness to mastery. Each one builds on the last. You don't skip ahead. You don't rush. You build — and every block you build gives you something that stays.

scenes.title: For Everyone
scenes.narration: You don't need to be fit. You don't need to want to fight. You need to be willing to learn. That's the only entry requirement.
scenes.learningObjective: Remove barriers — this is for you

scenes.title: Hong Kong
scenes.narration: Cuban method. Hong Kong home. Basic Reflex.
